quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all areas around your vehicle. There are blind spots that mirrors cannot see. Before changing lanes, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check these areas.

questions.question: What must you do when a school bus ahead on your side of the road has red lights flashing?

options.text: Slow down to 10 mph or less.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights on a school bus mean the bus is loading or unloading students. You must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing. Never pass a school bus that is picking up or dropping off students.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Prescription drugs are safe to drive on if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can both impair your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and other conditions. It is illegal to drive while under the influence of any drug that impairs your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: What should you do if you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog indicates that a pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must yield the right-of-way to any pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: If you start to turn but change your mind, what should you do?

options.text: Complete the turn.
Signal and rejoin traffic in your original lane.
Quickly steer back into your original lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the turn.
questions.explanation: Once you start turning, complete the turn. Suddenly steering back into your original lane can cause collisions with other vehicles.

questions.question: At what speed can hydroplaning start to occur?

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when there is standing water on the road. At speeds up to 35 mph, tires can move water away from the tire. Above 35 mph, tires cannot move the water as well. Your tires may lose grip on the road.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drinking alcohol and driving?

options.text: You can drive safely if you can walk in a straight line.
Your driving is not impaired if you are under the legal blood alcohol limit.
Alcohol damages judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol damages judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs your judgment. Good judgment is essential to react properly to things on the road. Even below the legal blood alcohol limit, any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: When should you yield your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Yield your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent collisions.

questions.question: What speed should you drive when merging onto the freeway?

options.text: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
Slower than the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is moving faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What speed should you drive when merging onto the freeway?

options.text: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.
The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, drive at or near the speed of the traffic around you.

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending soon.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow means two things: the protected turn is ending, and you must be ready to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
Point your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and put the vehicle in park when parked on a hill. Turn your front wheels toward the curb (downhill) or away from it (uphill) to help prevent rolling if the brakes fail.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if cars are approaching.
Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Drive carefully through without always stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: An octagon sign means stop. Come to a complete stop at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk or before the intersection. Then go only when it is safe.

questions.question: You approach an intersection with a flashing red light. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, check for traffic, then go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for traffic, then go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Treat it like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Roads are slippery when rain first starts. What should you do?

options.text: Do not make fast turns or stops.
Test your tires going uphill.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not make fast turns or stops.
questions.explanation: Wet roads reduce tire traction. Drive slower and avoid fast turns or sudden stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Turn only when the intersection is clear and it is safe.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When tailgated, create extra space in front and slow down gradually. Do not brake suddenly. This gives you room to stop safely.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Passing cars.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles driving straight. Turn only when you can safely do so without affecting oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what lights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog. High beams reflect back and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: If weather or darkness requires you to use lights while driving, which should you use?

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect back and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: If a car is following you too closely on a multilane highway, you should:

options.text: Speed up to match the speed of the car behind you.
Move to the right lane and let the car pass.
Slow down to annoy the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane and let the car pass.
questions.explanation: If a car follows you too closely on a multilane highway, move to the right lane to let them pass. On multilane roads, the left lane is for faster vehicles to pass slower vehicles.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross the street in the middle instead of using a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Must stop for them.
Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians. Even if they are crossing illegally, you must still stop for them.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers upset about slow traffic.
Make driving inconvenient.
Keep traffic out of dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic out of dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. When you approach a work zone, watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. These warn you and help direct traffic.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue causes mistakes with speed and distance judgment. It increases your crash risk and slows your decision-making. When tired, you could fall asleep at the wheel and crash, hurting or killing yourself or others.

questions.question: This sign is a:

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. There may be a change in traffic direction, a steep hill, or another dangerous situation that needs your attention.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill coming up. Slow down to avoid crashes and brake damage.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lane markings mean:

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The right lane may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate lanes with traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check for vehicles only in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a full stop and check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.question: Trucks' blind spots are:

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the left side of the cab.
On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots. The driver cannot see your car behind them, and you cannot see traffic ahead if you drive too close behind a truck. If the driver cannot see your face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light, you should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: Follow a police officer's directions. Their instructions override traffic signals and signs.

questions.question: How do you avoid glare from headlights of an approaching car?

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Stay focused on the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Do not look at the bright lights of an oncoming vehicle. Instead, glance toward the right side of the road. Then look ahead again to watch the other vehicle's position.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
Approaching vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect light back into your eyes. Use low beam headlights instead.

questions.question: When should you use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: In rain, snow, or fog, other drivers have a hard time seeing your vehicle. Headlights make your vehicle easier to see. If you need to use windshield wipers, you must also turn on your low beam headlights.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, or vehicles towing trailers may not see you directly behind them. Stay farther back when following these vehicles. Large vehicles can also block your view of the road ahead. Extra distance helps you see around them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Upcoming downgrade or hill.
Road construction area.
Upcoming narrowing of roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming downgrade or hill.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a steep or long hill ahead. The hill may have sharp curves.

questions.question: What should you do when a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Glance toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night—this can blind you. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: When should you use turn signals when parking next to a curb?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
Only when pulling next to the curb.
When pulling next to or away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling next to or away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Always use turn signals when pulling next to a curb or pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
No U-turns.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign is a traffic law that you must obey. It means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: How can you help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while in a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
When the yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
When the yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side can pass if it is safe to do so. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.
